objective: Bind the option-expiration-week calendar-effect candidate family (8 primary + 12 placebo) to verified source cards before handing the 20-candidate batch to the screening lane for K1/K2 testing against S3, resolving reports/research/harvest/directions.jsonl's dir:option_expiration_week_calendar_effect.

sources.core_claim: Long-only S&P 100 stocks during the option-expiration week (3rd-Friday week), cash otherwise. Backtest 1988-2010 (source paper Stivers & Sun 2013): 9.3%/yr, Sharpe 0.61, vol ~8.7%, MDD -15.14%.
sources.reflection: Sample is old (ends 2010, 15+ years before this iteration's anchor window) and the page discloses no recent-period figure; the local backtest under this project's own cost/fill contract is the decisive test, not this number.

sources.core_claim: Stivers & Sun (2013), J. Banking & Finance 37(11):4226-4240, 'Returns and option activity over the option-expiration week for S&P 100 stocks' -- the original academic paper behind Quantpedia's summary; abstract-level record located via WebSearch, cross-checking Quantpedia's characterization of the mechanism (delta-hedge rebalancing, reduced short-stock hedge positions during the expiration week).
sources.project_applicability: Independent confirmation that Quantpedia's summary accurately reflects a real, published academic finding, not a practitioner-invented rule.
sources.reflection: Full text is paywalled and was not fetched (abstract-level WebSearch summary only); does not change the local test's decisiveness.

sources.core_claim: Garcia-Ares & Muravyev (2025): option-return-anomaly predictability concentrates on the 3rd-Friday expiration and especially the following Monday (covered-call-writer rollover order imbalance). Sample May 2005-Dec 2021, robust throughout.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds the OPEX_*_WEEKMON candidates' deferred exit (captures the following-Monday effect).
sources.reflection: Studies delta-hedged OPTION returns, not stock/ETF direction -- used only as recent, independent mechanism support, not as a stock-return Sharpe number. Full text extracted via curl+pdftotext after WebFetch failed to parse the binary PDF.

sources.core_claim: 12 placebo candidates (PLACEBO_W{1,2,4}_{SPY,QQQ,DIA,IWM}) apply the identical construction anchored to non-expiration Friday weeks, to test whether the 3rd Friday specifically carries edge.
sources.project_applicability: Falsification design for the 8 primary candidates; itself never eligible for a keep tier.
sources.reflection: Not an external source; required because the frozen research protocol (G3-equivalent additional internal check per the queue task) asks for a placebo on the calendar-selection risk specific to this rule.

sources.core_claim: Per a WebSearch summary only (direct fetch blocked by a bot-verification wall): the option-expiration-week effect 'appears to be fading in recent years... has deteriorated over the last four years.'
sources.project_applicability: Counter-evidence motivating why this iteration treats its own 2024-2026 local backtest as decisive, not an assumption that Quantpedia's historical figures transfer.
sources.reflection: BLOCKED: could not independently re-read the full page; carried only via WebSearch's own summary, disclosed as such rather than dropped.

sources.core_claim: 'During 1983-2008, average option expiration week returns are relatively high for the S&P 500 Index and for large-cap stocks, but not for small-cap stocks.' A reader critique argues a volume-ratio-conditioned version is 'unusable in practice'.
sources.project_applicability: Supports restricting the universe to large-cap/index ETFs (SPY/QQQ/DIA/IWM), consistent with the queue task's own design.
sources.reflection: Own sample ends 2008; does not itself settle whether the effect still clears costs in 2024-2026 -- another reason the local backtest is decisive.

sources.core_claim: Official Cboe rule: monthly options expire the third Friday of the month; if that Friday is a holiday, expiration shifts to the preceding trading day.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms the holiday-handling convention used by entry_dates_for_friday/exit_dates_same_week.
sources.reflection: Highest-credibility source in this brief (primary regulatory text); directly validated against this iteration's own calendar logic and unit tests.

sources.core_claim: 0DTE S&P 500 index options have grown large enough that options-market-maker gamma hedge-rebalancing materially affects index volatility.
sources.project_applicability: Caveat: modern (0DTE-heavy) market microstructure differs from the Stivers & Sun (1988-2010) and early Garcia-Ares-Muravyev (2005-2021) samples.
sources.reflection: Does not directly study the weekly calendar effect; used only to motivate treating the local 2024-2026 backtest as decisive.

candidate_matrix_revisions: Initial preregistration: 20 candidates, 8 primary OPEX_{SPY,QQQ,DIA,IWM}_{WEEK,WEEKMON} plus 12 placebo PLACEBO_W{1,2,4}_{SPY,QQQ,DIA,IWM}. No revision yet; this is the first and only candidate list for this batch -- the screening lane must not add, remove or retune any candidate after seeing a result.
